title: Oily Tender Indian Katsuobushi Paratha
description: A briny, tender, and indulgent Indian dish featuring katsuobushi, sashimi-cut and ayurvedic-sattvic-friendly, wrapped in a form of paratha.
instructions: Mix 2 cups whole wheat flour and 1 cup water to make the dough for paratha.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and cover it with a damp cloth.
Divide the dough into 4 equal portions.
Roll out each portion into a thin circle.
Brush each paratha with 1/2 tsp ghee, 1/2 tsp kalonji oil, and a pinch of turmeric powder.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook each paratha for 1-2 minutes on each side.
While cooking the parathas, mix 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala powder, and 1 tsp lemon juice.
Once the parathas are cooked, brush them with the spice mixture and sprinkle with chopped cilantro.
In a separate pan, toast the katsuobushi over low heat until it's lightly browned and fragrant.
Once the katsuobushi is toasted, chop it into sashimi-cut pieces.
To assemble the dish, place a portion of the toasted katsuobushi in the center of each paratha, followed by a dollop of fresh ginger paste.
Fold the paratha in half and serve.
